title: Advancing Statistical ALCHEMI: Efficient Dopant Distribution Analysis at nm-scale from Sparse Spectrum Observations
content: Determining the dopant distribution is crucial for optimizing material performance, since its distribution in host crystals influences the chemical and electronic properties of materials. In electron microscopy, a technique called atom location by channeling-enhanced microanalysis (ALCHEMI) was developed to study substitutional elements in crystal samples by observing energy-dispersive X-ray spectra (EDS) [1] or electron energy-loss spectra [2]. Here, spectrum is observed by changing an incident beam direction around Bragg diffraction under a systematic condition. ALCHEMI was extended to Statistical ALCHEMI (St-ALCHEMI), where an incident beam is tilted at many directions around a zone-axis and observed spectra are statistically analyzed to determine dopant concentration [3]. For low dopant concentration, a total experimental time to collect spectra at many beam directions becomes long, typically several hours.
